references.text: Matthew tells us that Jesus went to Galilee after John had been put in prison ([ref:Matt 4:12|Matthew 4:12]). The Gospel of John clarifies here that the events in John 3 took place before this imprisonment.
Matthew describes how Herod arrested John and put him in prison ([ref:Matt 14:3-5|Matthew 14:3-5]). This is the imprisonment to which John 3:24 refers as not yet having occurred.
Mark mentions that Jesus came to Galilee after John had been handed over ([ref:Mark 1:14|Mark 1:14]). The Gospel of John places its narrative chronologically before this event.
Mark tells us that Herod sent men to arrest John and put him in prison ([ref:Mark 6:17|Mark 6:17]). John 3:24 emphasizes that this had not yet happened at that time.

Luke reports that Herod put John in prison because he had been rebuked by him ([ref:Luk 3:19-20|Luke 3:19-20]). The Gospel of John makes clear that the events in chapter 3 occurred before this imprisonment.

The preceding context tells us that Jesus and his disciples were in the region of Judea and baptizing, and that John was also baptizing at Aenon near Salim ([ref:Joh 3:22-23|John 3:22-23]). Verse 24 explains that this could happen because John had not yet been imprisoned.
